Thanks Olivia — we're on this. I'm attaching a first-pass acceptance_matrix.xlsx and a draft promptset_v3.json (the variant we'd like to test A/B). High-level proposal below so we can iterate quickly: 

Acceptance matrix (draft):
- Primary signal: end-to-end Task Completion Rate (TCR) mapped to the customer KPI (Acme support resolution in first message). Baseline: 92%
- Secondary signals: intent precision (threshold >= 90%), hallucination rate (<= 1.5% sampled), median latency <= 350ms
- Statistical threshold: minimum 95% confidence with uplift >= +1.5% to consider promotion
- Rollback triggers: any drop in TCR > 3 percentage points sustained over 24 hours or a single-day drop > 5 points

A/B plan (canary):
- 1% traffic to variant for 48 hours (smoke), then 5% for 7 days if no alerts
- Cohorts by locale and support channel to avoid mixed signals
- Monitoring: live dashboard with TCR, intent precision, hallucination sampling, and token cost per request

Owners / asks:
- Jonas: confirm monitoring metric names and alert thresholds (I used placeholders)
- Markus: confirm rollout constraints (batching/cache effects, KV cache warmup)
- Marissa / Stephanie: we need customer channels and escalation playbook confirmed

I've linked the Jira and the Drive sheet. I'm flexible on the confidence threshold if research recommends a different approach.

Attachments: acceptance_matrix.xlsx (draft); promptset_v3.json (draft)

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Operations

Agree with Kim's structure. Couple of notes from product/observability side: 

- For the primary metric, we should tie TCR to a deterministic downstream event in Acme's telemetry (ticket closed with resolution tag). If Acme's client-side instrumentation is inconsistent we should fallback to an internal surrogate.
- For statistical tests, prefer sequential testing with an alpha spend plan rather than a single 95% batch test; gives faster signal on streaming canary. We can use Bayesian credible intervals if Acme prefers continuous decision-making.
- Canary sizing: the 1%->5% ramp is fine, but require a minimum of 8000 requests per cohort to get meaningful intent precision estimates for low-frequency intents.

I'll sync with Observability to name the metrics and create the alert rules.

-Jonas
Product Lead, Evals
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Technical constraints and cautions: 

- KV cache warmup: when we switch prompt variants the cache hit-rate will drop; initial latency and token consumption will spike. Recommend a short warmup window (24-48 hours at low traffic) and exclude the first 24 hours from statistical comparisons.
- Batching/cost signals: the cost-per-request delta should be tracked; depending on prompt length we may see +12-20% unit token cost. Include cost per resolved ticket as a business signal.
- Canary fallback logic: plan a staged automated fallback (immediate rollback on critical alert OR timed rollback after N failures) and a human-in-the-loop approval for promotion. We need an SRE runbook entry.

I'll prepare a short infra checklist and the SRE runbook snippet.

-Markus
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

Adding customer context from our side: Acme's support traffic spikes weekday mornings (PDT) and we saw the largest TCR drop during those windows. They are sensitive to any regressions (renewal conversation later this quarter).

Proposed escalation playbook (short):
- Canary alarms to both Redwood CS and Acme PM; immediate traffic cut to 0% if TCR drop >5 pts OR hallucination >2% in sampled checks
- Auto-rollback enabled for critical conditions; otherwise, manual rollback within 1 hour of alert
- Compensation conversation: we should pre-authorize a credit band if regression confirmed against our rollout (finance sign-off needed)

I'll coordinate the customer comms and confirm which Slack channel we use for incident updates.

-Steve (Stephanie)
